title: The transfiguration part 1
scripture_text: ‘’From then on Jesus began to tell his disciples plainly that it was necessary for him to go to Jerusalem, and that he would suffer many terrible things at the hands of the elders, the leading priests, and the teachers of religious law. He would be killed, but on the third day he would be raised from the dead. But Peter took him aside and began to reprimand him for saying such things. “Heaven forbid, Lord,” he said. “This will never happen to you!” Jesus turned to Peter and said, ‘’Get away from me, Satan! You are a dangerous trap to me. You are seeing things merely from a human point of view, not from God’s. Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If any of you wants to be my follower, you must give up your own way, take up your cross, and follow me. If you try to hang on to your life, you will lose it. But if you give up your life for my sake, you will save it. And what do you benefit if you gain the whole world but lose your own soul? Is anything worth more than your soul? or the Son of Man will come with his angels in the glory of his Father and will judge all people according to their deeds. And I tell you the truth, some standing here right now will not die before they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.” Six days later Jesus took Peter and the two brothers, James and John, and led them up a high mountain to be alone. As the men watched, Jesus’ appearance was transformed so that his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as light. Suddenly, Moses and Elijah appeared and began talking with Jesus. Peter exclaimed, “Lord, it’s wonderful for us to be here! If you want, I’ll make three shelters as memorials—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” But even as he spoke, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is my dearly loved Son, who brings me great joy. Listen to him.”The disciples were terrified and fell face down on the ground. Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” he said.“Don’t be afraid.” And when they looked up, Moses and Elijah were gone, and they saw only Jesus.’ As they went back down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Don’t tell anyone what you have seen until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.” Then his disciples asked him, “Why do the teachers of religious law insist that Elijah must return before the Messiah comes?”Jesus replied, “Elijah is indeed coming first to get everything ready. But I tell you, Elijah has already come, but he wasn’t recognized, and they chose to abuse him. And in the same way they will also make the Son of Man suffer.” Then the disciples realized he was talking about John the Baptist.’’
devotional:
As Christians, many of us want a faith that is simple and straightforward with no uncertainty, no confusion, no doubt, and few questions. We are the ‘sat-nav’ generation who want to be told how to reach our destination with the least amount of trouble or hardship. And we have adopted the same kind of ’sat-nav’ attitude when it comes to our faith and our relationship with Jesus. We want the quickest and easiest way to spiritual maturity. We want God to tell us every turn we should make, we want our relationship with Jesus to be free from complications, conflict and confusion. We want a faith that is neat and sorted, we want a life free from mystery and ‘lostness’. But, as we are going to see, sometimes our relationship with Jesus is all about uncertainty.

In Matthew 16 we read the back story of the Transfiguration of Jesus which is recorded in chapter 17:1-13. A number of things happen that help us understand the Transfiguration.

1. Peter confessed that Jesus was the Messiah the Son of the living God.

This was one of the high points in the Gospel, Peter was beginning to understand who Jesus was. God the Father was teaching Peter. We will soon see that although Peter had received a revelation from God the Father about his Son Jesus, Peter’s understanding of Jesus was still incomplete.

2. Jesus began to teach the disciples about his suffering and death.

Now here was the problem, in the mind of Peter and the other disciples there was no room for a suffering Messiah. Reading Matthew 16:22 you get the impression that Peter was angry with Jesus, The NLT reads ‘Peter took him aside and corrected him. ‘Heaven forbid, Lord. This will never happen to you.’ The word the NLT translates correct is epitimaō, which has a technical meaning: it is used in Greek religion of gaining control over a spirit or a demon. Robert Guelich (Word Biblical Commentary: Mark.)

3. Jesus had to rebuke Peter by referring to him as a stumbling block, who was under the influence of Satan.

This must had been a real shock to Peter; although Peter may have meant well, Jesus could see the work of Satan behind what Peter had said.

4. Jesus begins not only to talk about his cross and his suffering, but he speaks about their suffering and their cross.

We are so familiar with these verses that they do not shock us the way they would have shocked these first disciples. These disciples had seen the Roman crosses on the side of the roads, they had seen the tough death many had suffered. And now Jesus their Messiah wanted them to carry their cross, a symbol of defeat and shame? One of the songs we sing is ‘This is amazing grace.’ One of the lines is about Jesus bearing our cross, I understand the sentiment behind the words, but Jesus bore our sin so we could bear our cross. We have been designed to live cross shaped lives, it would be a cruel injustice for God to take our ‘cross’ from us.

5. Jesus promised that some of his disciples would see him come in glory in Matthew 16:27-28.

There has been a lot of debate about these verses but I think, given the context, that they are referring to Jesus’ Transfiguration. They are also Jesus expressing a pastoral concern, this is how Jesus wanted to deal with the challenges that his disciples were facing regarding their relationship with him.
prayer: Father thank you that while carrying our crosses will be difficult in this life, one day we will all be able to see your glory.
